question: Fill in the blank: The ____ List in Schedule VII covers subjects of national importance such as defence.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Union**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India’s Constitution divides legislative powers between the Union and State governments through three lists: Union List, State List, and Concurrent List mentioned in Schedule VII.
 
• The Union List comprises subjects of national importance like defence, foreign affairs, atomic energy, and railways. Only the Parliament has exclusive power to legislate on matters listed under the Union List.
 
• Defence falls under the Union List as it requires a uniform and centralized approach to ensure national security and sovereignty.
 
• Currently, the Union List contains 97 subjects, making it the most extensive list in Schedule VII.
 
• Examples of subjects under the Union List include banking, insurance, communication, and citizenship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **State List:**

 
 
• The State List contains subjects of local or state importance, such as police, public health, agriculture, and irrigation.
 
• State governments have exclusive legislative authority over matters listed in the State List.
 
• Currently, the State List consists of 66 subjects.
 
• Examples: Markets and fairs, state taxes, and regulation of mines and minerals within the state.
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List:**
 
 
• The Concurrent List contains subjects where both the Union and State governments can legislate. However, in case of conflict, Union law prevails.
 
• This list includes subjects of shared interest such as education, marriage, and adoption.
 
• Currently, the Concurrent List contains 47 subjects.
 
• Examples: Criminal law, forests, and social security.
 
 
 
• **Residuary Powers:**
 
 
• Residuary powers refer to subjects not mentioned in any of the three lists. The Constitution grants the Parliament authority over these matters.
 
• Examples include cybersecurity, internet-related issues, and space exploration.
 
• Residuary powers ensure that emerging areas and unforeseen subjects are effectively governed by the Union government.
